title: Stack physics
description: What a pcb's stack means for the signals and the heat on it, as constants: the dielectric's permittivity until a reader says otherwise, how a neighbour lowers a track's impedance, light's speed, how a pcb gives off heat, and the widths searched for an impedance. Data, beside this class (#SECTION); the copper's and the pcb's thickness are its way of making, not this.

$schema.description: the schema this file is written to

source.description: where each value comes from: the papers, books and makers it is read from

permittivity.description: the dielectric's relative permittivity until a reader says otherwise

pair.description: how much a neighbour lowers a track's impedance, by how the track stands: 2·Z·(1 − share·e^(−decay·gap/reach))

additionalProperties.description: How a neighbour lowers a track's impedance.

share.description: how much of a track's impedance a neighbour takes at no gap

decay.description: how fast that falls as the gap grows, against the track's reach

freeSpace.description: the impedance of free space, ohms

surfaceCoefficient.description: watts a square metre of pcb gives off per kelvin

searchWidths.description: The widths searched for an impedance, millimetres, and how finely.

least.description: the narrowest width searched, in millimetres
